uncited: Data preprocessing prepares raw volumetric or projection data for optimization by normalizing physical quantities and constructing sparse-view inputs.
It solves the problem of inconsistent scales and insufficient angular coverage in sparse-view tomography and inverse rendering.

It differs from [Volume Normalization](1823-volume-normalization.md) by handling the initial conversion from raw intensity to physical attenuation and global scaling, and from [Geometric Normalization](12018-geometric-normalization.md) by focusing on intensity and view subsampling rather than coordinate system alignment.

**Inputs:** Raw projection images $I_v$, air-scan intensity $I_0$, scan metadata (source-to-detector distance, source-to-object distance, detector pixel pitch, rotation axis), and optionally ground-truth geometry (point clouds or meshes).
**Outputs:** Normalized attenuation projections, sparse-view subsets, and sampled supervision points.
*   **Supervision Points:** List of $(x, y, z)$ coordinates and associated labels (SDF, DDF, or ray hits).
